programme.title: Metric asset contract and Glessner comparison slice
programme.scope: Anchor every reusable part in metres with explicit grade/sill/storey datums; declare family parameters, sockets, material slots, stable component IDs, deterministic seeds and source/confidence attributes. Preserve the canonical Glessner asset. Prove a small 1808 frontage assembly beside it at street-eye and oblique views. Components: wall thickness; sill datum; eave/ridge datum; opening cutouts; handed variants; local/ENU placement; scale/UV contract.
programme.accept: No scale drift, hidden origin offsets or duplicated boundary faces; record baseline asset hashes and full/light mesh/texture costs.

programme.title: Stone, mortar and dressed masonry materials
programme.scope: Provide rock-faced granite, warm brown sandstone, pale limestone/Lemont or Bedford variants, smooth dressed trim and foundation rubble, each with clean albedo, normal and roughness plus physical joint/edge profiles. Granites must not be painted onto every mansion. Components: stone courses; ashlar corner bonds; rusticated base; mortar recess; voussoir texture orientation; coping; sparse chipped edges.
programme.accept: Render rough wall plus smooth carving on the 1808 exemplar in raking and diffuse light; metric grain, subdued roughness and nonrepeating courses match scale.

programme.title: Pressed, common and rough brick materials
programme.scope: Red pressed face brick, buff/common service brick, dark fired variants and Mayer rough/chipped brick; correct bonds, corner returns, soldier/segmental heads, mortar colour and shallow relief. Separate body clay from dirt. Components: brick bond; specials; string course; corner return; arch brick; soot/damp mask; back wall variants.
programme.accept: Build a facade/service-wall comparison on a named target; no Glessner courtyard colour applied indiscriminately, no checkerboard randomisation.

programme.title: Period roof coverings and drainage
programme.scope: Slate rectangular/scalloped courses, documented terracotta tile only where supported, copper sheet/standing seams, lead/zinc/painted metal flashings, bounded low-slope service roof. Add gutters, outlets, downpipes and boots. Components: slate exposure/lap; cut edges; hip/ridge caps; valley flashing; dormer apron; gutter bracket; downpipe shoe.
programme.accept: Roof sample spans daylight and grazing angles with no oversized tiles, baked highlights or zipper-like seam shadows; drainage ends at actual ground.

programme.title: Mansard, hip, gable and tower roof construction
programme.scope: Build data-driven roof planes and explicit valley/intersection trimming, convex/concave mansards, ordinary/stepped/ogee gables, polygonal/conical towers, dormers and chimney penetrations. Components: roof graph; fascia; soffit; verge; dormer cheeks; ridges; valleys; cross-gable return; watertight closure.
programme.accept: Demonstrate one representative house roof without roof planes crossing gable faces, floating cornices or doubled coplanar surfaces. This directly carries the lesson of Glessner repairs.

programme.title: Windows, glazing and visible interior depth
programme.scope: Rectangular sash, paired sash, segmental/round/pointed heads, transoms/fanlights, basement lights, grouped attic windows, limited leaded lights. Real wall openings, jambs/reveals, separate sash and glass with dark enclosed backing. Components: sash rails/stiles; muntin patterns; sill drip; arch spring; glazing plane; blinds; curtain edges; window well.
programme.accept: At 2-5 m the opening reads as a recess, glass reflects/transmits plausibly and blinds remain behind it; zero floating painted rectangles or unbounded transparency sorting.

programme.title: Entrances, stoops, porches and carriage doors
programme.scope: Single/double panel doors, vestibules, timber/glazed doors, deep arched entrances, historic carriage leaves/hardware, stone straight/curved stoops, porch floors/posts and basement stairs. Components: door leaf; rail/stile; lock/hinge; transom; threshold; tread/riser; cheek wall; handrail socket; porch skirt.
programme.accept: Prototype touches grade and floor correctly and clears public walks; carriage opening has thickness and lintel, not a texture panel. Keep accessibility to the walk renderer functional.

programme.title: Bays, oriels and towers
programme.scope: Rectangular, canted and bowed bays; full-height projections and corbelled upper oriels; circular/polygonal corner towers; copper caps and independent facade openings. Components: plan polygon/radius; floor bands; piers; corbels; bay roof; wall interface; upper support.
programme.accept: A canted and a curved example preserve measured footprint and window rhythm without faceting at near view; light tier retains their silhouette.

programme.title: Carved entrances and classical or Gothic trim
programme.scope: Parametric arch rings/voussoirs, moulding sweeps, lintels/hoods, colonnettes, column bases/capitals, Gothic tracery/crockets and original bounded foliate relief. Components: arch radius/rise; reveal; column order; capital profile; leaf relief; panel depth; repeated/unique motifs.
programme.accept: Compare a bespoke hero entrance and a restrained rowhouse surround. Generic carvings may support uncertain houses but cannot replace distinctive documented landmark carving.

programme.title: Cornices, parapets, dormer faces and cresting
programme.scope: Bracketed timber/metal cornices, dentils, friezes, classical entablatures, carved stone parapets, balustrades, urns, pediments, shaped gable copings and roof cresting. Components: bracket spacing; soffit; dentil; coping; baluster; urn; finial; cresting panel; dormer pediment.
programme.accept: Continuous corner returns, no hanging ends or roof clashes; unique Wheeler/Mayer profiles authored from evidence rather than scaling a generic gable.

programme.title: Ironwork, gates, canopies and boundary walls
programme.scope: Cast/wrought iron fence panels, spear/scroll variants, posts/piers, entry gates and hardware, area grilles, balcony/stair rails, iron-and-glass canopy and brick/stone boundary walls. Components: panel rhythm; picket section; rail joint; gate swing; hinge; wall cap; pier urn; canopy rib.
programme.accept: Silhouette reads at walking distance without wire shimmer; separate property patterns and height evidence; no fence crossing entrances or shared carriage drives.

programme.title: Coach houses, stable fittings and service wings
programme.scope: One/two-storey brick/frame/mixed service buildings, hay/loft doors, carriage bays, sash, roof ventilator only when supported, ramps, lean-tos and connecting wings. Components: rear footprint; party wall; carriage aperture; loft hatch; stable basement ramp; service stair; wall return.
programme.accept: Demonstrate one complete alley asset with all elevations and believable workyard connection; 1911 garage/auto labels are not 1904 use evidence.

programme.title: Conservatory and greenhouse assemblies
programme.scope: Modular iron/timber glazing bars, curved roofs, pitched bays, lanterns, masonry plinths, doors, gutters and restrained internal plant backing. Site-specific Pullman shapes remain authored. Components: glasshouse bay; curved rib; ridge vent; lantern; plinth; door; gutter; low-detail glass substitute.
programme.accept: Glazing and frame hierarchy remain legible in browser; avoid overlapping transparency and a full interior plant scene; validate a Pullman service-garden bay.

programme.title: Age, surface variation and ground contact
programme.scope: Shared authored material variants, roof/ground contact occlusion, mortar weathering, restrained soot near chimneys, water trails beneath outlets, timber grain/paint and yard surface transitions. Components: age mask; rain mask; soot; grass edge; masonry plinth dirt; path wear; independent per-property seed.
programme.accept: Condition represents each building in 1904, not modern ruin. Compare new Georgian work with 20-40-year-old houses under identical neutral lighting, preserving material identity.

programme.title: Chimneys, flues and roof service details
programme.scope: Brick and dressed-stone stacks, corbelled caps, documented clay pots, grouped flues, crickets and stepped flashing. Respect source-specific number, height and position; a chimney is a major skyline feature, not a randomly scattered prop. Components: shaft width/height; corbel courses; cap projection; flue opening; pot profile; roof penetration; flashing steps; soot direction.
programme.accept: Demonstrate ordinary service stack and Sherman carved stack with credible roof junction, dark recessed flues and source-bounded silhouette; reduced tier retains location and height.

programme.title: Frame cladding and exterior timber construction
programme.scope: Clapboard and board-and-batten families, supported decorative shingles, corner boards, water tables, timber fascia/brackets, porch lattice and pierced Gothic woodwork.
